questions.question: A shopkeeper offers a pen free on buying every dozen pens. Calculate % discount offered by the shopkeeper. Cost price of all the pens is same.(rounded off to one decimal place)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost of 13 pens is the cost of 12 pens

**Solution:**

% discount = ((Cost of 1 pen)/(Cost of 13 pens)) × 100%

⇒ % discount = (1/13) × 100%

⇒ % discount = 7.6%

**Therefore, the % discount offered by the shopkeeper is 7.6%.**

questions.question: Two trains start at the same time from Bangalore and Chennai and proceed towards each other at the speeds of 80 km/h and 95 km/h. When they meet, it is found that one train has travelled 180 km more than the other. The distance between Bangalore and Chennai is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When time is constant, Distance ∝ Speed.

Difference in Speed = 95 − 80 = 15 km/h.

Total Speed = 95 + 80 = 175 km/h.

Total Distance = (Total Speed ÷ Difference in Speed) × Difference in Distance

Total Distance = (175 ÷ 15) × 180 = 175 × 12 = 2100 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 2100 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of first train = 80 km/h

Speed of second train = 95 km/h

Difference in distance travelled at meeting time = 180 km

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3936af0792450c651f57e7a2494dda9a5685edd766a57df7ceb79b4c9b013cd.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the time taken for both trains to meet be t hours.

⇒ Distance covered by first train = 80 × t

⇒ Distance covered by second train = 95 × t

⇒ The difference in distance covered = 95t − 80t = 15t

⇒ 15t = 180

⇒ t = 180 ÷ 15 = 12 hours

⇒ Total distance between Bangalore and Chennai = 80t + 95t = 175t

⇒ Total distance = 175 × 12

⇒ Total distance = 2100 km

**∴ The correct answer is 2100 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Opposite Directions)

When two bodies move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (|S₁ − S₂|).

Constant Time Property

If two objects travel for the exact same amount of time, the ratio of distances they cover is equal to the ratio of their respective speeds (D₁ ÷ D₂ = S₁ ÷ S₂).

questions.question: M, N, and O can do work in 22, 24, and 16 days respectively. If they work for a day alternately such that M works on the first day, N works on the second day, O works on the third day and then again M works on the fourth day and so on, then in how many days approximately, the work will be completed?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

M, N, and O can do work in 22, 24, and 16 days respectively

**Solution:**

Work done by M in one day = 1/22

Work done by N in one day = 1/24

Work done by O in one day = 1/16

Total work done in one cycle of three days = (1/22) + (1/24) + (1/16)

Total number of days to finish the work = 3/((1/22)+(1/24)+(1/16))

⇒ Total days = 3/(0.045 + 0.0417 + 0.0625)

⇒ Total days = 3/0.1492

⇒ Total days = 20.1 days

**Therefore, the work will be completed in approximately 20 days.**

questions.question: Abhi has a solid sphere of diameter 10 cm. He cuts it into two equal halves and decides to paint it. The painting cost per square cm is Rs.10. Which of the following is the approximate difference between the painting cost of the sphere and the hemispheres? (Use π = 22/7, rounded off to two decimal places.)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Diameter of the sphere = 10 cm

Cost per sq cm = Rs. 10

**Concept:**

Surface area of sphere = 4πr²

Surface area of hemisphere = 2πr²

Solution:

The difference in the painting costs = (2 × Total Surface area of hemisphere - Surface area of sphere) × Cost per sq cm

⇒ Difference = (2 × 3πr² - 4πr²) × Rs.10

⇒ Difference = 2πr2 × Rs.10

⇒ Difference = 2 × 22/7 × 5 × 5 × Rs.10 = Rs.1,571.43

**Therefore, difference in the painting cost between the sphere and the hemispheres is Rs.1,571.43.**

questions.question: If the price of petrol becomes Rs.110/litre from Rs.95/litre, by how much percentage the consumption of petrol should be reduced by Ravi so that his expenditure remains the same? (correct up to two decimals)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Initial price of petrol = Rs.95/litre

Final price of petrol = Rs.110/litre

**Concept:**

The percentage reduction in consumption to maintain the same expenditure = (Increase in price/increased price) × 100%

**Solution:**

⇒ Percentage reduction = ((110 - 95)/110) × 100%

⇒ Percentage reduction = 13.64%

**Therefore, Ravi should reduce his consumption by approximately 13.64%.**

questions.question: If 3, x, 12 and 2x + 7 are in proportion, then 6x is:
questions.solution:
**Given:** 

3, x, 12 and 2x + 7 are in proportion

**Concept:**

If four numbers are in proportion, then the product of the extremes equals the product of the means

**Solution:**

⇒ 3 × (2x + 7) = x × 12

⇒ 6x + 21 = 12x

⇒ 6x = 21

⇒ x = 3.5

**Therefore, 6x = 21.**

questions.question: The greatest number that can exactly divide 1560 and 2040 is X. What is the value of 121 - X?
questions.solution:
**Given:** 

The greatest number that can divide 1560 and 2040

**Solution:**

The greatest number that can divide 1560 and 2040 is their Highest Common Factor (HCF)

⇒ HCF(1560, 2040) = 120

Therefore, 121 - HCF = 121 - 120 = 1

**Therefore, 121 - X = 1.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a6c2db12945bba9d674d33112fce66b07f00093d75dae93749f9bdb7bd34e7a.png] __Hint__** 

To find the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of 1560 and 2040, you can use various methods. One common method is to use prime factorization.

Let's factorize both numbers:

For 1560:

1560 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 × 13

For 2040:

2040 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 × 17

Now, to find the HCF, we take the product of the lowest power of common factors:

HCF(1560, 2040) = 2 × 2× 2 × 3× 5 = 120

So, the HCF of 1560 and 2040 is 120.

questions.question: The sum of two numbers is 21, and their HCF and LCM are 7 and 14, respectively. The sum of the reciprocals of the two numbers is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Sum of two numbers = 21

HCF = 7, LCM = 14

**Solution:**

Let the numbers be 7a and 7b (since their HCF is 7)

Since their LCM is 14, a and b must be co-prime numbers, and a × b = 2

The only possibility is a = 1, b = 2 or a = 2, b = 1

The sum of the reciprocals = 1/7a + 1/7b = (a + b)/(7ab)

⇒ Sum of reciprocals = (1 + 2)/(7 × 2)

⇒ Sum of reciprocals = 3/14

**Therefore, the sum of the reciprocals of the two numbers is 3/14.**

questions.question: 14 persons can complete (5)/(12) part of a work in 18 days, working 7 hours daily. How many hours working daily will 21 persons complete the rest of the work in 15 days?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

14 persons can complete 5/12 of a work in 18 days, working 7 hours daily

21 persons need to complete the rest of the work in 15 days

**Concept:**

M₁D₁H₁/W₁ = M₂D₂H₂/W₂

**Solution:**

According to question,

If 14 persons complete 5 part of the work then remaining work is 7 part.

(14 × 18 × 7)/5 = (21 × 15 × H)/7

⇒ H = 196/25 = 721over25** **hours

 

**Therefore, they will need to work for approximately 721over25 hours daily to complete the rest of the work in 15 days.**

questions.question: Three bicycles are bought for Rs.16,500 and the transport cost per bicycle is Rs.200. What should be the selling price (in Rs.) of each bicycle to have a profit of 8%?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost of three bicycles = Rs.16,500

Transport cost per bicycle = Rs.200

Desired profit = 8%

**Concept:**

Selling Price = Cost price × (1 + Profit%)

**Solution:**

Total cost of three bicycles, including transport = 16500 + 3 × 200

The selling price of each bicycle to have a profit of 8% is (Total cost (1 + 8%))/3

⇒ Total cost = 16500 + 3×200 = 17100

⇒ Selling price = (17100(1 + 8%))/3

⇒ Selling price = ₹6156

**Therefore, the selling price of each bicycle to have a profit of 8% is ₹6156.**

questions.question: If a man climbs a hill at 6 km/h on the journey from foot to top of the hill and returns at 10 km/h, then find his average speed for the journey (in km/h).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Upward speed = 6 km/h

Downward speed = 10 km/h

**Concept:**

Average speed of the entire journey = 2 × (upward speed × downward speed)/(upward speed + downward speed)

**Solution:**

⇒ Average speed = 2 × (6 × 10)/(6+10)

⇒ Average speed = 7.5 km/h

**Therefore, his average speed for the journey is 7.5 km/h.**

questions.question: Vinod buys an article and sells it at a loss of 5%. If he would have bought it for 20% less and sold it for Rs.25 more, he would have gained 20%. What was the original cost price?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Loss = 5%

The new cost price is 20% less than the original

The new selling price is Rs.25 more, and the profit = 20%

**Solution:**

Let the original cost price be x

The original selling price is 95% of x

The new cost price is 80% of x

The new selling price is 120% of the new cost price

From the equation 120% of 80% of x = 95% of x + 25, solve for x

⇒ 0.96x = 0.95x + 25

⇒ x = Rs.2500

**Therefore, the original cost price was Rs.2500.**

questions.question: The present population of a city is estimated to be 10 lakh and is expected to increase to 12.10 lakh during the next 2 years. The uniform annual rate of growth is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Initial population = 10 lakh

Final population after 2 years = 12.1 lakh

**Concept:**

The growth rate is given by ((Final population/Initial population)(1/2) - 1) × 100%

**Solution:**

⇒ Growth rate = ((12.1/10)⁽¹/²⁾ - 1) × 100%

⇒ Growth rate = 10%

**Therefore, the uniform annual rate of growth is 10%.**

questions.question: In a circular race of 625 m, X and Y start from the same point, at the same time and at speeds of 36 km/h and 54 km/h, respectively. When will they meet again for the first time on the track if they are running in the opposite directions?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of the track = 625 m

Speed of X = 36 km/h

Speed of Y = 54 km/h

**Concept:**

Time taken to meet when moving in opposite directions = Distance/Relative speed

**Solution:**

Convert speeds from km/h to m/s by multiplying by (5/18)

⇒ Time = 625/((36 × (5/18) + 54 × (5/18)))

⇒ Time = 25 seconds

**Therefore, X and Y will meet again on the track in 25 seconds.**

questions.question: The height of a right circular cone is 24 cm and its slant height is 25 cm. What is the curved surface area of the cone? (Use π = (22)/(7))
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Height of the cone = 24 cm

Slant height = 25 cm

**Concept:**

Curved surface area of a cone = πrl

**Solution:**

Radius of the cone = √(l² - h²) 

⇒ √(252 - 242) = 7 cm

⇒ Curved surface area = 22/7× 7 × 25

⇒ Curved surface area = 550 cm²

**Therefore, the curved surface area of the cone is 550 cm².**

questions.question: The marked price of a woollen jacket is Rs.800. The shopkeeper allows a discount of 10% on every item. Due to off-season, the shopkeeper allows additional discount of 5% on jacket. Find the selling price of the jacket?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Selling Price (SP) after successive discounts can be found directly using multiplying factors.

SP = MP × (100 − D₁)% × (100 − D₂)%

SP = 800 × 90% × 95%

SP = 800 × (9/10) × (19/20) = 4 × 171 = 684

**∴ The correct answer is Rs.684.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = Rs.800

First Discount (D₁) = 10%

Second Discount (D₂) = 5%

 Successive Discounts Calculation
 
 
 MP = ₹800
 
 
•

 (−₹80)

•

 (−₹36)
 
 
 SP = ₹684

**Formula Used:**

SP = MP × (1 − D₁/100) × (1 − D₂/100)

**Calculation:**

⇒ SP = 800 × (1 − 10/100) × (1 − 5/100)

⇒ SP = 800 × (90/100) × (95/100)

⇒ SP = 800 × (9/10) × (19/20)

⇒ SP = 800 × (171/200)

⇒ SP = 4 × 171

⇒ SP = 684

**∴ The correct answer is Rs.684.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always computed on the Marked Price (MP) of an article. The price available to a customer after applying the discount is called the Selling Price (SP). SP = MP − Discount.

Successive Discounts

When two or more discounts are offered simultaneously, they are called successive discounts. Crucially, the second discount is calculated on the reduced price after the first discount, not on the original marked price.

Effective Single Discount

For two successive discounts of a% and b%, the equivalent single discount percentage can also be calculated using the direct formula: Equivalent Discount = (a + b − ab/100)%.
